title: Existence of K-flat resolutions on a ringed site
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a site and $\mathcal O$ a sheaf of commutative rings on $\mathcal C$. For every cochain complex $\mathcal G^\bullet$ of sheaves of $\mathcal O$-modules [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules] there exist a K-flat complex $\mathcal K^\bullet$ [def-pc-kflat-complex] whose terms are flat $\mathcal O$-modules [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules] and a quasi-isomorphism $\mathcal K^\bullet\to\mathcal G^\bullet$ [def-pc-quasi-iso-modules] which is surjective in every degree.

proof.text: Construct the tensor-hom adjunction for coefficient-universe-r sheaves of modules. Essential smallness of the site makes the local hom modules r-small; shrink these modules, transport restriction maps, and transfer their sheaf condition. Curry and uncurry presheaf-linear maps, then use sheafification to obtain the adjunction. This construction is proved locally in the Lean module and does not identify the site object, site morphism, or coefficient universes.

Sheafify the free presheaf on the underlying sections of each module. Evaluation is an epimorphism and is natural, while the free presheaf is sectionwise flat. The monoidal sheafification comparison and finite-limit preservation transfer flatness to its sheafification, giving a functorial flat cover. Integer-indexed colimits of module sheaves are exact by the exact forgetful functor to sheaves of abelian groups. Apply the existing reduced left-resolution construction to the inclusion of flat modules: its resolution augmentation is a quasi-isomorphism, its terms are colimits of flat modules, and its resolution complex is categorically K-flat. Use the underlying resolution API directly rather than the wrapper that assumes a Grothendieck instance in the hom universe. These deductions and category hypotheses are proved in the item module from the source library and Mathlib.

Choose a flat epimorphism q_i:Q_i to G^i for every integer i. Explicitly construct D with D^i=Q_i direct-sum Q_(i-1) and differential from the first summand identically into the next second summand. Sending the second summand back to the preceding first summand is a contracting homotopy. The maps [q_i,q_(i-1) followed by d_G] define a chain map a:D to G which is epi in each degree. Set K=P direct-sum D and f=[p,a]. Inclusion and projection, together with this contracting homotopy, exhibit P and K as homotopy equivalent, and the inclusion followed by f is p. Consequently f is a quasi-isomorphism and is epi in every degree. Finite sums of flat objects are flat, so all terms of K are flat. These formulas and identities are proved directly, without a boundedness assumption.

Categorical K-flatness descends to the homotopy category, hence transfers to the epicified resolution along the homotopy equivalence of step 3. For an acyclic Z, the map from the zero complex to Z is a quasi-isomorphism. Tensoring it on the right with the resolution remains a quasi-isomorphism by categorical K-flatness. Its source is zero because tensoring is additive, so its target is acyclic. This is IsKFlatIndependentCoefficients. The right half of termwise categorical flatness supplies exactly the required exactFunctor assertion for tensorRight in each degree.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_isKFlatResolutionIndependentCoefficients
    {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [EssentiallySmall.{r} C]
    {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
    [J.HasSheafCompose (forget₂ CommRingCat.{r} RingCat.{r})]
    [J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{r}]
    [HasSheafify J AddCommGrpCat.{r}]
    {R : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{r}}
    (G : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{r}
      ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat.{r} RingCat.{r})).obj R)) ℤ) :
    letI := SheafOfModules.isMonoidal_W_independentCoefficients R
    ∃ (K : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{r}
      ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat.{r} RingCat.{r})).obj R)) ℤ)
      (f : K ⟶ G), CochainComplex.IsKFlatIndependentCoefficients K ∧
        (∀ i : ℤ, exactFunctor _ _
          (@MonoidalCategory.tensorRight _ _ (SheafOfModules.monoidalCategory R) (K.X i))) ∧
        QuasiIso f ∧ (∀ i : ℤ, Epi (f.f i))
